$comment: GENERATED from docs/harness/profiles by compose-harness-config.mjs. Policy lives in the adapter baseline (playwright.json); project and lane facts live in the profile (playwright-boilerplate). Re-compose after editing either, then run npm run harness:sync.

pipeline.title: Requirements and scope
pipeline.does: Collect the product requirements from every declared source and reconcile them into one PRD that fixes the scope. Record conflicts and gaps between sources instead of resolving them silently.

pipeline.title: Scenarios
pipeline.does: From the approved scope, list the happy, negative, and edge scenarios. Each one cites its acceptance criterion and the source that shows the behavior.

pipeline.title: Test plan
pipeline.does: From the approved scenarios, plan the testing in sections by format. For each section say what it covers, which lane owns it, what is out of scope, and the environment and data it needs.

pipeline.title: Test cases
pipeline.does: From the approved plan, write detailed cases that cover each flow end to end. Read the specs and the code, and check existing automation first: mark every case new, extended, or already covered, and never duplicate coverage.

pipeline.title: Implementation
pipeline.does: Implement only approved cases, following the framework's architecture and rules. Reuse existing commands, helpers, and fixtures before adding new ones. A human approves the exact diff, every changed file, before any test runs against it.

pipeline.title: Execution
pipeline.does: With G4 holding, run the focused tests first, then the impacted regression checks, using the project's own commands.

pipeline.title: Debugging
pipeline.does: Diagnose each failure from its evidence and fix the root cause, not the symptom. A fix changes the approved diff, so G4 is approved again before the rerun.

pipeline.title: Evidence
pipeline.does: Record the runs as evidence and link every case to its requirement. A human approves the evidence; without it the work is not complete.

pipeline.title: Validation
pipeline.does: Reconcile the results against the approved scope, scenarios, plan, and cases, and list every gap. An independent reviewer judges this stage, not the author.

pipeline.title: Release
pipeline.does: With G5 holding, prepare release material only. A human decides, performs, or authorises the release: an agent never publishes, merges, or deploys.

devPipeline.title: Requirements and scope
devPipeline.does: Collect the requirements from every declared source into one PRD that fixes the scope and the acceptance criteria. Record conflicts and gaps between sources instead of resolving them silently.

devPipeline.title: Design
devPipeline.does: From the approved scope, decide the approach: components touched, interfaces and contracts, data and migration changes, security and performance impact, rollout and rollback. Reuse what exists before adding anything new.

devPipeline.title: Plan
devPipeline.does: From the approved design, list the tasks and, for each acceptance criterion, the behaviors to prove (B-1, B-2, ...) with the test that proves each one and the regression area it touches.

devPipeline.title: Tests first
devPipeline.does: Write the failing test for each planned behavior before any implementation and record the red run (commit trailer `Harness-Phase: red B-n`). The human approves the tests and their failure output.

devPipeline.title: Implementation
standards: smallest change that turns each test green
no new suppression, debugger or ticketless TODO
devPipeline.does: Make each failing test pass (`Harness-Phase: green B-n`), then refactor with the tests green. A human approves the exact diff, every changed file, before verification runs against it.

devPipeline.title: Verification
devPipeline.does: With G4 holding, run the project's own standard (lint, type-check, unit, integration) and the impacted regression checks, using the project's commands.

devPipeline.title: Debugging
devPipeline.does: Diagnose each failure from its evidence and fix the root cause, not the symptom. A fix changes the approved diff, so G4 is approved again before the rerun.

devPipeline.title: Evidence
devPipeline.does: Record the verification runs and link every behavior to its requirement and its test. A human approves the evidence; without it the work is not complete.

devPipeline.title: Review
devPipeline.does: An independent reviewer reconciles the diff against the approved scope, design, and plan, and lists every gap. The author never reviews their own change.

devPipeline.title: Release
devPipeline.does: With G5 holding, prepare release material only. A human decides, performs, or authorises the release: an agent never publishes, merges, or deploys.

research: no implementation without a follow-up plan

rules.instead: waitForResponse() or a deterministic expect() assertion
rules.why: A fixed delay hides the real readiness condition and flakes in CI.
rules.message: Hard wait detected. Use a response wait or state-based assertion.

rules.never: a selector literal in a spec or helper
rules.why: A UI change should have one owner, not scattered copies.
rules.message: Hardcoded selector. Use a UI config constant.

rules.never: a route or endpoint literal when config exists
rules.why: Routes and API contracts need one maintained registry.
rules.message: Hardcoded route or endpoint. Use the config registry.

rules.never: page-object classes, action layers, or wrappers outside helpers/
rules.why: A second UI abstraction duplicates config and helper ownership.
rules.message: Page-object or action-layer dependency. Use the helper-first architecture.

rules.never: a password, secret, API key, or token assigned a literal string
rules.instead: environment variables loaded from a gitignored .env or CI secret
rules.why: A committed credential is a breach, not a style issue.
rules.message: Hardcoded credential. Read it from the environment instead.

rules.why: Authentication should be isolated and cached, not repeated in every test.
rules.message: Per-test login detected. Use storageState setup instead.

rules.never: a spec importing test directly from @playwright/test
rules.why: The fixture is the single injection point for helpers.

rules.never: POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE in a smoke spec
rules.instead: read-only assertions; put mutations in e2e coverage
rules.why: Smoke coverage must be safe against shared and production-like environments.
rules.message: Write request in smoke suite. Smoke tests must remain read-only.

rules.never: a SQL literal in a spec or helper
rules.instead: a frozen entry from playwright/configs/db/** passed to the db fixture
rules.why: A query is the datastore contract. One schema change should mean one config edit, not a grep across specs.
rules.message: Hardcoded SQL. Move the query to playwright/configs/db/** and use the db fixture.

rules.never: test.only()/test.describe.only(), or skip/fixme without a recorded quarantine
rules.instead: run focused tests only from the CLI; put // @quarantine ISSUE-123: reason directly above a deliberate skip or fixme
rules.why: A focused test can hide suite failures, while an unrecorded skip hides risk with no owner.
rules.message: Focused test or unrecorded quarantine. Remove .only; a skip/fixme needs // @quarantine ISSUE-123: reason directly above it.

rules.never: skip semantic locators without a reason
rules.why: Semantic locators are more stable and accessible.

rules.never: use first() or nth() where a filter can identify the element
rules.why: Index-based locators silently target the wrong element when the UI changes.
rules.message: Narrow the locator with a filter before using an index.

rules.never: a new config, helper, or spec without searching first
rules.instead: search literal selectors, routes, and endpoints by value
rules.why: Duplicate owners cause the same app change to need multiple fixes.
rules.message: Search the configs and helpers by value before creating a new asset.

rules.never: a test with no requirement tag, more than one, or an unknown id
rules.instead: exactly one known requirement id in the title and as a tag, plus Type, Priority, and tier tags
rules.why: The title survives every reporter and the tag supports filtering; together they make coverage computable.
rules.message: Test must carry exactly one known requirement id in its title and tags.

agents.name: project-bootstrapper
agents.description: Derive an approved project and application contract from verified sources before any test generation.
agents.when: Start a new project or module from no existing automation context

agents.name: playwright-test-automation
agents.description: Implement Playwright tests and helpers using the helper-first Config → Helpers → Tests architecture.
agents.when: Build a requirement-backed helper-first Playwright module

agents.name: playwright-bug-hunter
agents.description: Debug a failing Playwright test, trace root cause, and propose an exact compliant fix.
agents.when: Trace and repair a failing test

agents.name: pre-merge-qa-gate
agents.description: Evaluate supplied change and command evidence through the complete 6-phase pre-merge QA gate.
agents.when: Evaluate supplied diff and verification evidence and return the final QA verdict
agents.readOnlyRationale: Read/search only by design: the gate cannot edit files or execute shell commands, so the builder never grades its own output.

agents.name: playwright-cli
agents.description: Use Playwright CLI for token-efficient browser discovery, debugging, and codegen-first scaffolding.
agents.when: Use CLI-first browser discovery or codegen

agents.name: pr-creator
agents.description: Create a pull request with the repository's standard generated description.
agents.when: Opening a pull request with a generated description

agents.name: workflow-maintainer
agents.description: Simplify repository workflow scripts, agents, skills, and docs without duplicating ownership.
agents.when: Simplify workflow scripts, agents, skills, or docs
